transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess… I’m here because I can’t really sit still. Like in the radiology suite or in class, I feel like I’m crawling out of my skin, and I end up pacing or shifting around, or finding reasons to get up. I tried to just deal with it for months, but it hasn’t really stopped.
Has this restlessness been causing you a lot of distress or problems in your daily life?

Yeah… it has. My evaluations in the clinic have gotten worse, and I’m on a formal remediation plan now. Supervisors say I’m disrupting patient flow and making it harder to work as a team. I’m kind of worried that if I don’t get it under control, I could lose my spot in the program.
Did you experience these feelings of restlessness when you were a child, before you turned 12?

Yeah… I think so. My parents still bring up those elementary school meetings where teachers said I was always getting out of my seat, calling out, or rushing ahead before they’d finished directions. So it was definitely before middle school.
Do you often find yourself struggling to pay attention to details or making careless mistakes in your work or other activities?
I don’t know… not really in that way. I mean, I haven’t noticed a big issue with careless mistakes or missing details. It’s more… hard to say.
Do you often interrupt others or blurt out answers before they've finished speaking?

Yeah… I do that. Like if a supervisor’s explaining a positioning step, I’ll jump in before they’re even done, thinking I know what they’re asking. Then I realize I missed the part that actually mattered.
Do you often act on impulse without thinking, like grabbing something or doing something physical without considering the consequences?
I’m not really sure. I mean… I don’t think of it that way much. I guess I’d have to think about what you mean by “physical” stuff.
Do you often interrupt others or start tasks without being asked to, in situations that aren't physical, like in conversations or when working on projects?

Yeah… mostly in conversations or at work when someone’s explaining something. Like a supervisor will be going over a positioning step or asking me something, and I’ll answer before they finish. Then I realize I missed the important part.
Do you often have trouble following through on instructions or finishing tasks?
I’m not sure. I mean… maybe sometimes, but I don’t really track that. It depends what the task is, I guess.
Do you often have trouble organizing your tasks or activities?
I don’t know… I guess I haven’t really paid attention to whether it’s organizing or just, like, getting started. I can’t say for sure.
Do you often blurt out answers or interrupt others in non-physical situations, like in meetings or conversations?
Yeah… I do. Like if a supervisor’s explaining a positioning step or asking me something, I’ll jump in before they’re done. Then I realize I missed the part that actually mattered.
Do you often find yourself easily distracted by things around you?
I don’t really know. I mean, I notice things around me, sure, but I haven’t really paid attention to whether it distracts me a lot.
Do you often find yourself having trouble sustaining focus during tasks or activities?
I’m not really sure. I mean, sometimes tasks feel hard to stay with, but I haven’t paid close enough attention to say it’s a regular thing.
Were you more often running, climbing, or physical in play as a child than other kids you knew?

I don’t really remember if I was more like that than other kids. What I do know is now, when I’m supposed to sit still in class or in the radiology suite, I feel really restless… like I need to move, so I end up shifting around or pacing if I can.
As a child, did you often engage in running or climbing activities more than your peers?

I don’t really remember the running or climbing part as a kid. What I know is now, if I have to sit still in the radiology suite or class, I feel like I’m crawling out of my skin. I try to deal with it, but I still end up shifting around or pacing if I can.
Do you often have trouble paying attention to details or following through on instructions in your daily activities?
I don’t know. I haven’t really noticed that as a big thing, honestly. I’d have to think about it more.
Do you often find yourself daydreaming or having difficulty staying focused on the task at hand?
I’m not really sure. I mean, I zone out sometimes like anyone does, but I haven’t really noticed it being a major thing.
Do you often find yourself having trouble staying focused on what someone is saying to you?
I’m not sure, honestly. I don’t think I’ve noticed that happening a lot… maybe sometimes, but nothing that really stands out to me.
Have you often had difficulty sustaining attention in tasks or play activities?
I’m not sure. I don’t really think of that as something I struggle with a lot… maybe here and there, but nothing I can point to specifically.
Did you have more energy or fidget more than other kids when you were younger?

Yeah… probably. My parents still bring up stuff from elementary school, like teachers saying I was always getting out of my seat or calling out. I guess I’d rush ahead before they finished directions too. So… yeah, it was there pretty early, not just recently.
Do you often have difficulty waiting for your turn in line or in other situations?

Yeah… I guess so. Waiting my turn, like in lab practice or when I’m waiting for a machine to open up, I get really edgy. I’ll keep stepping forward or checking the time, and sometimes I ask if I can go next. I’ve been called out for it a couple times.
